question: Which symptom is a classic sign of an underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism)?

options.A: A fast and pounding heartbeat
options.B: Shaking hands and muscle tremors
options.C: Intolerance to cold temperatures
options.D: Sudden and unexplained weight loss

explanation: You nailed it! When the metabolism slows down due to low thyroid hormone, patients feel chilly even when everyone else is warm.

question: Why is a risk assessment done before holding a mass gathering?

options.A: To reduce ticket prices for attendees
options.B: To eliminate the need for any on-site security personnel
options.C: To identify potential hazards and plan appropriate medical and safety responses
options.D: To guarantee that the event makes a substantial financial profit

explanation: Spotting trouble spots beforehand means we can get medical help and safety measures ready before any emergency strikes.

question: Why is it smart to set a clear hypothesis before starting a nursing research project?

options.A: It guarantees that the intervention will be successful
options.B: It eliminates the need for any statistical analysis later
options.C: It guides the study design and data collection methods
options.D: It replaces the requirement for an ethical review board

explanation: A clear hypothesis gives your project a roadmap so you know exactly how to gather your data and test your ideas.

question: How does surveillance help us check if a vaccination campaign worked?

options.A: By calculating the exact salary of the nurses giving the shots
options.B: By showing whether disease rates drop after the vaccines are given
options.C: By tracking how many nurses attended the training workshop
options.D: By testing the chemical composition of vaccine vials

explanation: By keeping track of sickness rates over time, public health teams can easily tell if giving out those vaccines actually stopped the disease.

question: Which heart rhythm is a life-threatening emergency that requires immediate CPR and defibrillation?

options.A: Atrial fibrillation
options.B: Premature atrial contractions
options.C: Ventricular fibrillation
options.D: Sinus bradycardia

explanation: Ventricular fibrillation (V-fib) is a true medical emergency! The lower chambers just quiver instead of pumping, meaning no blood flows. Quick CPR and a shock are literal lifesavers here.

question: What is a major direct consequence of unsafe abortion resulting from an unintended pregnancy?

options.A: Severe hemorrhage and sepsis
options.B: Sudden adult onset diabetes
options.C: Chronic kidney stone formation
options.D: Permanent loss of eyesight

explanation: Unsafe abortions frequently lead to dangerous complications like severe bleeding and life-threatening infections. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h2)

question: What is a major risk associated with using social media networks during a fast-moving crisis?

options.A: The rapid spread of unverified rumors and false information
options.B: High costs charged to citizens for reading emergency alerts
options.C: The complete inability to transmit text messages or pictures
options.D: Government blockades that stop all communication instantly

explanation: Social media allows anyone to post instantly, which can lead to panic if false reports circulate before officials verify them. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T9#GNS315_U5_T9_h5)

question: Why is it much harder to get an exact, consistent dose from herbal medicines compared to factory-made tablets?

options.A: Government regulations strictly forbid the weighing of plant roots
options.B: Active ingredient levels vary based on soil, weather, and plant maturity
options.C: Herbal remedies lose all chemical potency within two hours of harvest
options.D: Traditional healers refuse to use measuring spoons and cups

explanation: Mother Nature doesn't use a laboratory scale! Plants grow differently depending on the soil and weather, meaning the strength of the active ingredients changes from one harvest to the next.

question: Why do healthcare professionals use standardized anatomical terminology?

options.A: To replace traditional nursing assessment skills
options.B: To make medical records longer and more detailed
options.C: to confuse patients so they ask fewer questions
options.D: To prevent misunderstandings during clinical communication

explanation: Standardized terms give everyone a universal vocabulary so patient care details are never misunderstood across different shifts or teams. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T2#GNS111_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why do people with common colds frequently develop sinus headaches and pressure?

options.A: The brain increases blood flow to the sinuses to fight off the virus
options.B: Cold air freezes the fluid inside the sphenoid and frontal cavities
options.C: Swollen nasal linings block the tiny drainage openings of the sinuses
options.D: Excess mucus production physically shatters the underlying skull bones

explanation: When swelling closes off the narrow ostia, mucus gets trapped inside the sinus cavities, causing pressure to build up and trigger pain. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T3#GNS211_U4_T3_h4)

question: What is a major danger of a severe Vitamin A deficiency in young children?

options.A: Extreme weight gain and early childhood obesity
options.B: Permanent softening of the bones resembling rickets
options.C: Uncontrolled bleeding due to lack of blood clotting factors
options.D: Increased risk of severe infections like measles and blindness

explanation: Vitamin A is a hero for eye health and immunity. Without it, kids are much more vulnerable to serious infections like measles, plus vision problems.

question: How do medications help manage hormone hypersecretion when surgery isn't an option?

options.A: By permanently destroying all blood flow to the kidneys
options.B: By replacing the target tissues with artificial skin
options.C: By blocking hormone receptors or inhibiting hormone synthesis
options.D: By stimulating the pituitary gland to make even more hormones

explanation: If surgery is off the table, drugs step in to either stop the gland from making the hormone or block target tissues from responding to it. Smooth thinking! [learn more](GNS211_U1_T7#GNS211_U1_T7_h5)

question: What is the minimum recommended physical distance between residents in shared quarantine facilities?

options.A: No distance restriction is needed
options.B: One arm length or less
options.C: Exactly fifty centimeters
options.D: At least two meters

explanation: Maintaining a distance of two meters helps prevent the spread of respiratory droplets between individuals. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h5)

question: What is the main difference between a hypertensive urgency and a hypertensive emergency?

options.A: The patient's age and previous history of cardiac disease
options.B: The presence of acute target organ damage in emergencies
options.C: The absolute numerical reading of the diastolic blood pressure
options.D: The requirement for oral medication in emergency settings

explanation: You got it! An emergency means high blood pressure is actively damaging vital organs (like the brain or heart), whereas an urgency has high readings without active organ harm.

question: Which measure is best for protecting a DRF from internal fraud and missing stock?

options.A: Allowing pharmacy cashiers to set their own daily mark-up rates
options.B: Keeping all financial records hidden from the hospital management committee
options.C: Implementing regular internal audits and automated inventory tracking
options.D: Relying solely on verbal reports from the procurement officer

explanation: You guessed it! Regular audits and clear digital tracking leave a reliable paper trail, making it much harder for inventory or cash to go missing unnoticed.

question: What does accountability mean for a nurse unit manager regarding finances?

options.A: Personally paying for any broken equipment on the ward
options.B: Deciding how much profit the entire hospital should make
options.C: Setting the tax rates that fund the local health facility
options.D: Being responsible for staying within the assigned departmental budget

explanation: Accountability means managers must answer for how funds are spent in their unit and keep expenses within limits. [learn more](GST322_U2_T4#GST322_U2_T4_h2)

question: Why shouldn't a nurse rely on just one method to check a patient's nutrition?

options.A: Patients usually refuse to answer dietary recall questionnaires alone
options.B: Hospital policies strictly require at least four different diagnostic tests
options.C: Lab values and physical signs can be influenced by acute illness or hydration
options.D: Single methods are too expensive for routine primary health clinics

explanation: Things like fluid changes can mess with lab numbers quickly, so combining a few tools gives you a much clearer, more reliable picture.

question: What is the best feeding practice recommended for an infant's first six months of life?

options.A: Exclusive breastfeeding
options.B: Water and thin maize pap
options.C: Mashed family meals
options.D: Goat milk and infant formula

explanation: Correct! Breast milk alone provides all the water, nutrients, and antibodies a baby needs for the first six months. Nothing else is required! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h7)

question: What is a research checklist mainly used for in nursing studies?

options.A: To schedule nursing staff shifts on the ward
options.B: To systematically record observations and data
options.C: To prescribe medication dosages to patients
options.D: To diagnose complex medical conditions

explanation: Think of a checklist as your organized guide! It gives you a structured way to observe and tick off items uniformly during a study.

question: Why is independent clinical judgment especially important for a home health nurse?

options.A: Home health clients never require emergency medical intervention
options.B: Hospital protocols do not apply outside formal medical facilities
options.C: Families dictate the exact medical treatments the nurse must perform
options.D: Doctors and other supervisors are not physically present in the home

explanation: Exactly! When you are out in the field visiting a patient's home, you often work solo. Your own assessment skills and quick thinking are key to spotting any health changes. Great job!

question: Why does a requisition form need a supervisor's review and signature before heading to the store?

options.A: To stop nurses from talking to warehouse workers
options.B: To delay delivery and keep storerooms empty
options.C: To give the medical director extra paperwork to sign
options.D: To confirm that what you asked for matches your actual usage

explanation: Exactly! Authorization checks help catch mistakes, prevent over-ordering, and keep everything transparent.

question: A hospital notices multiple incident reports about look-alike drug vials. What is the best quality improvement action?

options.A: Stop ordering that medication entirely without finding an alternative
options.B: Instruct all nurses to read medication labels three times before work
options.C: Fire the nurses who reported the confusing packaging
options.D: Change how and where those specific drug vials are stored

explanation: Brilliant! Fixing the system—like changing drug storage or packaging—is way more effective than just telling staff to 'be careful.'

question: How does poor hospital infrastructure affect a nurse's daily shift?

options.A: It forces nurses to spend more time improvising care due to missing tools
options.B: It guarantees that nurses will receive higher hazard allowances
options.C: It reduces the total number of patients seeking medical attention
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for patient documentation

explanation: Nigerian nurses are masters of improvisation! When basic equipment is missing, you have to think on your feet to keep patients safe. That takes true skill.

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to changing health behaviors in a community?

options.A: Deeply rooted cultural myths and traditional practices
options.B: Language differences and lack of health literacy
options.C: Immediate access to fully stocked, free community pharmacies
options.D: Severe poverty making healthy choices unaffordable

explanation: You got it! Having easy access to free medical supplies actually helps people practice healthy habits rather than blocking them.

question: Who was a key pioneer of the Moral Treatment movement in France?

options.A: Sigmund Freud
options.B: Dorothea Dix
options.C: Florence Nightingale
options.D: Philippe Pinel

explanation: Philippe Pinel famously ordered the chains removed from patients in Paris asylums and introduced humane treatment. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T3#GNS314_U1_T3_h3)

question: Why does stopping your antibiotics halfway through a course cause drug resistance?

options.A: It immediately destroys all friendly bacteria inside the stomach
options.B: It causes the remaining tablets in the pack to expire faster
options.C: It triggers an allergic reaction when the drug is taken again
options.D: It leaves the strongest microbes alive to mutate and multiply

explanation: When you stop early, you only kill the weak germs. The tough ones survive, get smarter, and multiply—meaning that drug won't work for you next time!

question: Why should nurses tell patients not to chew gum or smoke while fasting for this test?

options.A: They mess up the laboratory machine used to spin blood
options.B: They can trigger digestion and change the blood sugar results
options.C: They cause severe dehydration that collapses arm veins
options.D: They immediately destroy all red blood cells in the body

explanation: Even tiny actions like chewing gum can trick the body into releasing insulin, throwing off the test results. Patient instructions matter!

question: Which part of Nigeria generally records lower modern contraceptive prevalence rates?

options.A: Major coastal ports
options.B: Capital city districts
options.C: The Southern zones
options.D: The Northern zones

explanation: National health surveys consistently show differences in mCPR across regions, with the northern zones generally recording lower rates than the southern zones.

question: Why is it important for researchers to discuss study limitations during data interpretation?

options.A: To prove that their research is completely flawless and superior
options.B: To justify increasing the budget for future research projects
options.C: To confuse readers so they do not question the findings
options.D: To honestly acknowledge any weaknesses or factors that could affect the results

explanation: No study is perfect, and transparency about limitations builds scientific credibility. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T1#GNS217_U3_T1_h6)

question: How should you, as a nurse, use data from a machine or diagnostic device?

options.A: Combine the machine data with patient history and physical assessment
options.B: Relies solely on the machine numbers without checking the patient
options.C: Record the numbers and discharge the patient immediately
options.D: Ignore the device data if it conflicts with a gut feeling

explanation: Machines are super helpful, but safe nursing means matching those numbers with what you actually see and hear when checking your patient!

question: What is the main goal of epidemiology in public health?

options.A: Manufacturing vaccines for global distribution
options.B: Managing financial budgets for health clinics
options.C: Treating individual patients in a hospital ward
options.D: Studying how and why diseases spread in a population

explanation: Epidemiology is all about looking at the big picture—how and why health issues affect entire populations, rather than just treating one patient at a time. Great job wrapping your head around this community health fundamental!

question: Why do some disaster survivors turn to alcohol or drugs months after the event?

options.A: Because social customs require drinking alcohol during holidays
options.B: To cure physical infections caused by contaminated floodwaters
options.C: As an unhealthy attempt to self-medicate untreated emotional pain
options.D: Because emergency relief supplies always include addictive drugs

explanation: Well reasoned! When professional mental health support isn't handy, some people sadly try to use substances to numb painful memories and calm their anxiety. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T3#GNS314_U6_T3_h6)

question: A patient vomits severely just two hours after eating leftover rice. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Primary viral lung infection
options.B: Food-borne intoxication
options.C: Parasitic bowel infestation
options.D: Chronic autoimmune reaction

explanation: Spot on! That super-short window between eating and vomiting is the classic signature of a food toxin (intoxication). Keep up the fantastic work!

question: What role does the environment play in keeping an endemic disease going?

options.A: It builds permanent immunity inside the bloodstream of the host
options.B: It provides external conditions that bring the agent and host together
options.C: It acts as the biological organism that manufactures the toxins
options.D: It develops pharmaceutical treatments to cure the infected population

explanation: Things like warm weather or stagnant water create the right setting for germs and vectors to find human hosts easily.

question: A nurse arrives in a disaster zone and needs to help set up safe drinking water and toilets. Which cluster should she connect with?

options.A: Emergency Shelter Cluster led by ICRC
options.B: WASH Cluster led by UNICEF
options.C: Health Cluster led by WHO
options.D: Logistics Cluster led by WFP

explanation: Spot on! WASH stands for Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene—making UNICEF the go-to team for clean water and sanitation needs.

question: Why must a researcher carefully explain how they chose their participants (sample selection)?

options.A: To make the research budget look much smaller than it is
options.B: To hide the identities of the nurses working on the ward
options.C: So others understand who was studied and can judge if results are fair
options.D: To ensure that only wealthy patients take part in the study

explanation: Being transparent about your participants builds trust and shows everyone that your results are reliable and unbiased.

question: Studying a rare medical condition, a researcher asks early patients to connect her with other patients they know. What technique is this?

options.A: Snowball sampling
options.B: Quota sampling
options.C: Stratified sampling
options.D: Systematic sampling

explanation: Spot on! Just like a snowball rolls and gets bigger, your participant list grows as each person refers you to the next.

question: Which of these situations is considered an intentional injury?

options.A: A youth falls off a moving commercial motorcycle and fractures a leg
options.B: A teenager gets stabbed during a street fight over money
options.C: A student drinks contaminated water and develops severe gastroenteritis
options.D: An adolescent accidentally touches a hot cooking stove and gets burned

explanation: Exactly! Assaults and physical fights are classed as intentional injuries because there is a deliberate human action meant to cause harm.

question: What gets squeezed flat against the tunica albuginea to trap blood inside the penis?

options.A: Subtunical venules
options.B: Dorsal nerve fibers
options.C: Cavernous arteries
options.D: Urethral glands

question: When preparing a weaker cream from a stronger stock, what is your very first step?

options.A: Identify the starting strength and your target strength
options.B: Measure the patient's daily fluid intake and output
options.C: Throw away half of the total stock bottle immediately
options.D: Add water directly into the manufacturer's original tube

question: Which of these is an environmental hazard that can cause falls at home?

options.A: Well-lit hallways
options.B: Secured handrails in bathrooms
options.C: Cluttered walkways and loose rugs
options.D: Low-heeled supportive footwear

explanation: Loose rugs and messy pathways are classic trip hazards. Clearing them is a simple and life-saving way to keep older adults safe from falls.

question: A dying patient says they are scared to die alone while family steps out. What should you do?

options.A: Tell them not to worry because family will be back tomorrow
options.B: Sit with them and offer a reassuring, calming presence
options.C: Run out to find the doctor right away
options.D: Tell them to think about happier times

explanation: Sometimes your physical presence is the best medicine. Just staying by their side chases away that terrifying loneliness.

question: How should you handle a patient who strongly resists making healthy lifestyle changes?

options.A: Demand immediate compliance because the nurse knows best
options.B: Discontinue all nursing visits until the patient changes their attitude
options.C: Acknowledge the patient's feelings and explore the root cause of hesitation
options.D: Threaten to report the patient to local health authorities

explanation: Commands and threats never work well in nursing. Partner with your patient, listen to their worries, and solve problems together.

question: What is the general outlook for a patient who gets steady medical and psychological care for OCD?

options.A: No change in symptoms regardless of what treatments are tried
options.B: A permanent and complete physical cure with zero future stress
options.C: Inevitably progressive mental decline requiring institutional care
options.D: Significant symptom reduction and improved daily functioning

explanation: Wonderful! With the right mix of therapy and medication, most patients find great relief and get back to enjoying their lives.

question: Why can a poor shift handover easily lead to a malpractice claim?

options.A: It automatically causes patients to fall out of their hospital beds
options.B: Crucial patient care details get lost, leading to missed treatments or delayed assessments
options.C: It forces doctors to perform nursing duties they are not trained for
options.D: It breaks hospital labor laws regarding nursing shift lengths

explanation: Good communication keeps patients safe! When handover is messy, important care steps get missed, which can harm the patient.

question: What is the main goal of Behaviour Change Communication (BCC) compared to basic health education?

options.A: Promoting and sustaining healthy community practices
options.B: Reducing the cost of pharmaceutical drugs
options.C: Writing medical records for hospital filing
options.D: Increasing the number of operating theatres

explanation: You got this! BCC goes beyond just sharing facts—it actively helps communities adopt and stick to healthy habits for the long run.

question: Why is long-term support still needed after active rehabilitation therapy ends?

options.A: To keep hospital bed occupancy rates artificially high
options.B: To ensure the patient remains dependent on healthcare workers
options.C: To help maintain functional gains and prevent secondary complications
options.D: To eliminate the need for home visits by family members

explanation: You nailed it! Ongoing follow-up stops setbacks like pressure sores or joint stiffness, helping individuals hold onto their independence for the long haul.

question: Why do nurses look at a patient's skin as a mirror of their inner health?

options.A: Skin changes often appear before systemic disease symptoms show
options.B: The skin controls all chemical reactions in the human body
options.C: External skin temperature dictates core metabolic rate completely
options.D: Internal organs directly push pigment through the dermal layers

explanation: The skin often gives us early warning signs. Changes in color, texture, or rashes can show up before other internal sickness symptoms even start!

question: How is explanatory research different from just watching patients in the ward?

options.A: Explanatory research requires no data collection from actual human subjects
options.B: Explanatory research looks for the underlying reasons behind an event, not just the facts
options.C: Observation is done by doctors while explanatory research is strictly for nursing students
options.D: Observation uses numerical data while explanatory research only uses spoken stories

explanation: Great thinking! While regular observation just shows us what is happening, explanatory research digs deeper to find the exact causes.

question: In Nigeria's routine immunization schedule, which vaccines are given right at birth?

options.A: Measles 1, Yellow Fever, and Meningitis

options.C: BCG, OPV 0, and Hepatitis B birth dose
options.D: Inactivated Polio Vaccine and Tetanus toxoid

question: What is the best way to document a skin lesion in a patient's chart?

options.A: Sketch the lesion on scrap paper and leave it unrecorded in charts
options.B: Use precise measurements, anatomical locations, and objective descriptive terms
options.C: Use general labels like 'large sore' to save time during documentation
options.D: Write brief personal opinions regarding the patient's personal hygiene

explanation: Be specific! Writing exact sizes, locations, and clear descriptions helps other nurses track if the wound is healing properly.

question: What is the primary goal of community health care financing?

options.A: To eliminate all taxes paid by citizens
options.B: To raise, pool, and allocate funds for health services
options.C: To replace government budgets entirely
options.D: To generate profit for private hospital owners

explanation: Financing systems focus on gathering resources and distributing them effectively so health services remain available to the population. [learn more](GST322_U4_T4#GST322_U4_T4_h1)

question: Your stroke patient has left-sided neglect. Where should you place their lunch tray?

options.A: Place the tray directly in the center without mentioning its location
options.B: Encourage the client to reach across their body to the left side
options.C: Place all food items and utensils on the client's right side
options.D: Feed the client entirely to avoid any missed food or frustration

explanation: Putting everything on their strong, unaffected right side makes sure they can actually see their food and eat independently, keeping them well-nourished and happy.

question: How do interferons protect your body from viral infections?

options.A: They wrap around viruses and digest them.
options.B: They raise body temperature to burn up viral particles.
options.C: They warn nearby healthy cells to put up their defenses against viruses.
options.D: They tell the bone marrow to make extra red blood cells.

explanation: Think of interferons as chemical text messages sent by infected cells to warn their healthy neighbors: 'A virus is coming, lock your doors!'

question: How do corticosteroids help patients with autoimmune diseases like lupus?

options.A: By calming an overactive immune system that is attacking healthy tissues
options.B: By destroying abnormal white blood cells in bone marrow
options.C: By rebuilding damaged joint cartilage and bone
options.D: By replacing lost vitamins in the blood

explanation: Spot on! In autoimmune conditions, the body attacks itself. Steroids act like a peacekeeper, calming down that overactive immune response.

question: What is the main purpose of conducting a hospital space audit?

options.A: To measure the exact weight of furniture located in administrative offices
options.B: To identify underutilized areas and evaluate how efficiently space is used
options.C: To determine the retail price of medical supplies sold to patients
options.D: To decide which clinical staff members deserve a salary increase

explanation: A space audit checks how rooms are actually being used so managers can make the most of current areas before deciding to build new extensions.

question: What best describes a laissez-faire leadership style?

options.A: Hands-off with minimal guidance
options.B: Voting on all ward decisions
options.C: Strict control over every action
options.D: Rewarding staff for good work

explanation: Laissez-faire leaders step back and give their team complete freedom and autonomy in how they do their work. [learn more](GST321_U3_T3#GST321_U3_T3_h4)

question: Why do hospitals still rely on high-temperature incineration for certain waste, despite environmental concerns?

options.A: It is the only method permitted for ordinary kitchen food leftovers
options.B: It transforms dangerous clinical trash into reusable office furniture
options.C: It requires zero financial investment to build and maintain
options.D: It completely destroys difficult pathological waste and reduces overall volume

explanation: Some body tissues and heavy clinical waste need intense heat to completely and permanently wipe out disease risks.

question: How can long-term chronic workplace stress affect an employee physically?

options.A: It causes permanent hearing loss
options.B: It can contribute to high blood pressure and sleep problems
options.C: It leads to immediate skin burns from acids
options.D: It causes instant bone fractures

explanation: When psychological pressure stays high for too long, the body reacts physically—often showing up as high blood pressure, sleeplessness, and constant fatigue.

question: Why are postnatal visits considered crucial shortly after childbirth?

options.A: To monitor maternal recovery and assess infant growth milestones
options.B: To collect hospital fees and issue birth certificates
options.C: To replace routine childhood immunization schedules
options.D: To schedule permanent family planning surgery for the father

explanation: Postnatal checks allow the nurse to monitor healing, check bleeding, and ensure the baby is growing and feeding well. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T7#GNS124_U2_T7_h4)

question: Why shouldn't a patient start long-term uric acid-lowering drugs right in the middle of a severe gout attack?

options.A: It can cause sudden shifts in uric acid levels that worsen or prolong the acute inflammation
options.B: The medications are completely inactive while the joint is red and swollen
options.C: It permanently destroys the effectiveness of the drug for future use
options.D: It causes immediate kidney failure if taken during joint pain

explanation: Starting these meds mid-attack can cause uric acid levels to swing abruptly, making the existing flare last even longer.

question: What is the main role of thrombin in the common pathway?

options.A: It prevents blood from clotting inside healthy vessels
options.B: It destroys excess platelets before they can form a plug
options.C: It causes smooth muscle in the vessel wall to relax
options.D: It converts soluble fibrinogen into insoluble fibrin strands

explanation: Thrombin acts as the key enzyme that turns liquid fibrinogen into solid fibrin threads to build the actual clot structure. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is the medical term for the hard bumps of urate crystals that form under the skin in long-standing gout?

options.A: Tophi
options.B: Vesicle
options.C: Nodule
options.D: Pannus

explanation: Tophi are those visible lumps of uric acid crystals that can pop up under the skin or around joints when gout isn't well controlled over time.

question: What is the main job of an Electronic Health Record (EHR) in a hospital or clinic?

options.A: To automatically prescribe medications without a doctor's order
options.B: To track the daily attendance and payroll of hospital staff
options.C: To store a comprehensive digital history of a patient's health information
options.D: To manage the public financial budget of the hospital

explanation: Correct! An EHR keeps all of a patient's medical history, test results, and treatments in one digital folder so authorized health workers can see them easily.

question: What is the main difference between incidence and prevalence?

options.A: Incidence is used for chronic diseases, while prevalence is for injuries
options.B: Incidence counts only new cases, while prevalence counts all existing cases
options.C: Incidence measures past history, while prevalence predicts future risk
options.D: Incidence requires a blood test, while prevalence is calculated by survey

explanation: Incidence tracks newly developing cases, whereas prevalence tracks the total burden of existing cases. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h5)

question: A clinic has skilled staff and modern equipment, but poor women in the community cannot afford the user fees. Which quality dimension is missing here?

options.A: Accessibility
options.B: Safety
options.C: Effectiveness
options.D: Efficiency

explanation: You got this! When financial barriers stop people from using available services, accessibility and equity are compromised. Care must be within reach for everyone.

question: What is the primary way researchers share their completed findings with the professional community?

options.A: Shredding documents to protect hospital secrets
options.B: Publishing articles in peer-reviewed journals
options.C: Telling patients secretly during hospital discharge
options.D: Posting personal opinions on social media apps

explanation: Peer-reviewed journals are the gold standard for distributing verified research to other professionals. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T1#GNS217_U3_T1_h7)

question: Why might a patient with salpingitis feel deep pelvic pain during sexual intercourse?

options.A: Vaginal contractions trap air inside the closed uterine cavity
options.B: Hormonal shifts completely stop natural vaginal lubrication
options.C: Pelvic thrusting puts pressure on inflamed, swollen fallopian tubes and surrounding tissues
options.D: The infection causes immediate dryness of the external labial skin

explanation: Movement during sex jostles the pelvic organs, which hurts when the tubes are already swollen, tender, and inflamed.

question: Why is helping clients connect with their community an important part of day and night hospital care?

options.A: It completely replaces the need for any ongoing medication
options.B: It reduces stigma and helps clients function within their social environment
options.C: It ensures patients never have to return to their families
options.D: It allows the hospital to discharge staff and save money

explanation: You got it! Keeping clients connected to their communities builds acceptance and supports long-term recovery.

question: Which standardized nursing terminology is used specifically to name clinical nursing diagnoses?

options.A: NANDA-I
options.B: NIC
options.C: NOC
options.D: ICD-10

explanation: Great nursing care starts with clear language! NANDA-I gives us the official framework for naming the human responses and health issues we diagnose and treat every day. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h2)

question: When reviewing literature, what do we call the missing or weakly studied areas in current research?

options.A: Financial grants
options.B: Research gaps
options.C: Patient registries
options.D: Nursing licenses

explanation: Spotting what is missing in current studies points directly to research gaps that need investigation. Great job thinking like a researcher!

question: What happens inside the body of a patient with severe burns that makes a high-protein diet critical for their survival?

options.A: Hypermetabolism causes rapid tissue breakdown and protein loss
options.B: Bones instantly release all stored calcium into the blood
options.C: The kidneys stop filtering waste products completely
options.D: The digestive tract absorbs fewer vitamins than normal

explanation: Severe burns put the body into an extreme 'overdrive' state where muscle and tissue break down rapidly. High protein helps fight off this severe wasting.

question: What happens to vital body proteins if the blood pH moves way outside the normal range?

options.A: They multiply rapidly to restore chemical balance
options.B: They convert directly into usable cellular energy
options.C: They bind permanently to excess sodium molecules
options.D: They denature and lose their functional shape

explanation: Proteins are picky! When blood gets too acidic or too basic, proteins change shape (denature) and stop working properly, which halts important body processes.

question: How do patient satisfaction surveys help a home health agency improve its care?

options.A: By serving as legal proof that no errors ever occurred in the home
options.B: By replacing all internal clinical audits and staff evaluations
options.C: By identifying operational weaknesses and areas needing service adjustment
options.D: By reducing the total number of patients assigned to each nurse

explanation: Listening directly to client feedback gives agencies clear insight into what's working and where care can be made even better.

question: Why do we often see long waiting lists in healthcare instead of a quick market balance?

options.A: Prices are often distorted or subsidized, causing demand to outstrip supply
options.B: Doctors refuse to treat patients until their medical conditions worsen
options.C: Patients prefer waiting months for elective procedures to save money
options.D: Hospitals deliberately hide available beds to inflate treatment costs

explanation: You nailed it. When care is heavily subsidized or cheap, everyone rushes in, and soon there are more patients than available beds or staff.

question: Why is batch cooking recommended as part of a family meal strategy?

options.A: It permanently eliminates the need to store food in a refrigerator
options.B: It ensures that all food cooked is consumed in one sitting
options.C: It provides quick, healthy meals for busy days and reduces reliance on fast food
options.D: It allows the cook to avoid washing dishes for an entire month

explanation: Preparing larger portions ahead of time saves valuable time on hectic days and prevents impulsive, less nutritious food choices. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T015#GNS227_U4_T015_h4)

question: A home health nurse notices an older patient's pension checks are missing and lights are cut off despite having funds. What is going on here?

options.A: Physical neglect
options.B: Active abandonment
options.C: Financial exploitation
options.D: Emotional maltreatment

explanation: Taking or misusing a vulnerable person's money or resources is financial exploitation. You're building great clinical intuition!

question: How does a work culture of punishment (blame culture) ruin clinical data?

options.A: Staff members spend too much time analyzing charts instead of nursing
options.B: Staff tend to hide mistakes, leading to inaccurate and incomplete data
options.C: Patients refuse to answer questions about their hospital stay
options.D: The hospital is forced to purchase expensive computer software

explanation: If nurses feel they will be punished for mistakes, they'll naturally keep quiet about them. When errors are hidden, our data becomes useless for fixing real problems.

question: Which lobe of the cerebral cortex is primarily responsible for processing visual information?

options.A: Occipital lobe
options.B: Parietal lobe
options.C: Temporal lobe
options.D: Frontal lobe

explanation: The back of the brain, known as the occipital lobe, specializes in receiving and making sense of what the eyes see. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T3#GNS211_U3_T3_h3)

question: What natural pain-relieving substance does the body release in large amounts during labour?

options.A: Growth hormone
options.B: Beta-endorphins
options.C: Antidiuretic hormone
options.D: Parathyroid hormone

explanation: The body is brilliantly designed! Beta-endorphins act as natural painkillers during labour by binding to special receptors in the nervous system.

question: What is the main goal of good nutrition for someone living with HIV?

options.A: To completely replace antiretroviral drugs
options.B: To support the immune system and enhance treatment
options.C: To prevent passing the virus to others
options.D: To guarantee permanent weight gain for everyone

explanation: Spot on! Good nutrition gives your body the strength to fight off infections and helps HIV medications work much better.

question: What do geographical boundaries (like rivers or roads) give to a traditional community?

options.A: Clear physical limits and a defined space for service delivery
options.B: Guaranteed financial funding from international agencies
options.C: Absolute immunity from infectious disease outbreaks
options.D: Complete isolation from neighboring populations

explanation: Physical borders make it easy for nurses to map out an area and plan where to bring healthcare services.

question: How does a sincere clinical apology usually affect an injured patient or their family?

options.A: It legally bars them from ever asking questions about the incident
options.B: It makes them completely forget that an adverse event occurred
options.C: It validates their suffering and often reduces feelings of anger
options.D: It forces them to discharge themselves from the hospital immediately

explanation: A respectful, honest apology lets patients know their pain is recognized. This often calms their anger and lowers the desire for aggressive lawsuits.

question: What is the underlying cause of Sheehan syndrome after severe childbirth bleeding?

options.A: Lack of blood supply causing pituitary gland tissue death
options.B: A severe kidney infection spreading from the uterus
options.C: Permanent nerve damage from regional anaesthesia
options.D: An autoimmune reaction attacking the thyroid gland

explanation: Extreme blood loss drops the body's blood pressure so low that the pituitary gland gets starved of oxygen and blood, leading to tissue death (necrosis) and hormone imbalances later.

question: Which activity is an example of non-structural disaster mitigation?

options.A: Installing steel reinforcement pillars in a hospital ward
options.B: Purchasing heavy-duty earthquake-resistant generators
options.C: Building a high concrete wall around a reservoir
options.D: Enforcing strict zoning laws to stop building in floodplains

explanation: That's right! Laws and policies are non-structural measures that guide us away from dangerous areas without physical building changes.

question: Why do nurses join in on nutrition education programs along with food distribution efforts?

options.A: To help local governments collect taxes on agricultural goods
options.B: To teach families how to make the most of affordable, local ingredients
options.C: To replace the need for physical food supply improvements
options.D: To ensure that families stop cooking traditional meals altogether

explanation: Education helps families build healthy, balanced meals using whatever cheap, local ingredients are available around them. You're crushing these!

question: In SMART goal setting for rehab, what does the letter 'M' stand for?

options.A: Manual
options.B: Measurable
options.C: Medical
options.D: Maximum

explanation: 'M' stands for measurable! It means you can actually track progress and see how far your patient has come. Easy peasy!

question: What does it mean when we say a nursing research problem must be empirically testable?

options.A: It requires no data collection from patients
options.B: It only relies on personal opinions and feelings
options.C: It has already been solved in past decades
options.D: The variables can be observed and measured

explanation: Empirical just means we can actually see, count, or measure it in the real world rather than just guessing or going purely on vibes!

question: What do we mean by the term 'hidden hunger' in teenage nutrition?

options.A: Eating enough calories to feel full, but missing vital vitamins and minerals
options.B: An eating disorder where teenagers hide food
options.C: Feeling constantly starved despite eating three big meals
options.D: An inability to feel full after eating fiber

explanation: Brilliant! Hidden hunger happens when your belly feels full, but your body is still starving for the micronutrients it needs to thrive.

question: A patient gets defensive and stops answering when asked about alcohol intake. What should you do first as a nurse?

options.A: Immediately discharge the patient from the ward without further care
options.B: Reassure the patient of confidentiality and use a calm, non-judgmental tone
options.C: Document in bold red ink that the patient is a violent criminal
options.D: Threaten to report the patient to the hospital management and security

explanation: Building a safe space of trust and zero judgment is key to helping patients lower their guard and share the truth about their health.

question: How does the endocrine system's signaling mainly differ from the nervous system?

options.A: Nervous signaling relies entirely on blood transport systems
options.B: Endocrine signaling uses fast electrical impulses directly to tissues
options.C: Nervous signaling controls long-term growth instead of rapid reflexes
options.D: Endocrine signaling is slower and provides longer-lasting control

explanation: While nerves give quick, snap reactions (like pulling your hand from fire), hormones take a bit longer to travel through the blood, but their effects stick around much longer. Great to know for clinical practice!

question: What is the main purpose of multi-sectorial collaboration during a disaster?

options.A: To allow different agencies to work as a unified front
options.B: To let the health ministry manage all rescue operations
options.C: To reduce the total number of volunteers needed
options.D: To ensure only government agencies handle relief funds

explanation: Disasters require many different groups to combine their strengths so they can respond effectively together. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h1)

question: Which blood tests are most commonly used to evaluate kidney filtration function?

options.A: Serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen
options.B: White blood cell count and hemoglobin
options.C: Serum electrolytes and platelet count
options.D: Prothrombin time and international normalized ratio

explanation: Creatinine and blood urea nitrogen are waste products filtered by the kidneys, making them reliable indicators of renal function. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T2#GNS213_U4_T2_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a common challenge faced by national disaster agencies?

options.A: Poor road networks and heavy traffic congestion during crises
options.B: Excessive funding and overabundance of modern rescue equipment
options.C: Infrastructural violations like buildings blocking natural waterways
options.D: Inadequate financial support and poor resource allocation

explanation: Sadly, disaster agencies usually struggle with a shortage of funds and equipment, rather than having too much! [learn more](GNS315_U1_T9#GNS315_U1_T9_h7)

question: What is the main goal of using patient assistive devices in healthcare?

options.A: To increase the cost of long-term care stays
options.B: To help patients maintain independence and safety
options.C: To reduce hospital administration paperwork
options.D: To completely replace the need for nursing staff

explanation: You got this! Assistive devices are designed to empower patients, helping them move and care for themselves safely and with dignity.

question: Why should NGOs involve community members right from the project planning stage?

options.A: It prevents the government from inspecting the clinic
options.B: It guarantees that the project will cost zero money
options.C: It ensures cultural acceptance and long-term success
options.D: It stops foreign donors from asking questions

explanation: Spot on! When community members help design a project, they feel proud of it and are much more likely to use and protect the service. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T6#GNS124_U2_T6_h6)

question: Why do healthy pregnant women need to produce more insulin as their pregnancy advances?

options.A: The growing fetus directly destroys maternal pancreatic cells
options.B: The liver stores less glucose as pregnancy progresses
options.C: Placental hormones make maternal cells more resistant to insulin
options.D: Maternal kidneys begin to excrete insulin much faster

explanation: As the placenta grows, it releases hormones that create insulin resistance, forcing the pancreas to pump out extra insulin to keep blood sugar stable. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T006#GNS226_U4_T006_h1)

question: What is a major limitation of relying only on BMI to judge someone's health?

options.A: It changes drastically depending on what the patient ate for breakfast
options.B: It requires expensive laboratory equipment to calculate properly
options.C: It only works accurately for newborn infants and toddlers
options.D: It cannot distinguish between weight coming from muscle mass versus body fat

explanation: Muscle weighs more than fat, meaning a very muscular athlete might show up as overweight on a BMI chart even when they are super healthy!

question: An asthmatic patient starts wheezing and coughing after spending the afternoon outside on a heavy smog day. What caused this attack?

options.A: Inflammation and bronchoconstriction caused by inhaled air pollutants
options.B: An allergic reaction to pollen-free chemical gases
options.C: A sudden bacterial invasion of the bloodstream
options.D: Complete destruction of the heart valves due to low oxygen

explanation: Correct! Smog irritates sensitive airways, making the muscles around them tighten up and swell, which triggers asthma symptoms.

question: Which management style best reflects the psychology part of Deming's framework?

options.A: Encouraging teamwork, reducing workplace fear, and respecting individual differences
options.B: Assuming staff only care about their end-of-month salary
options.C: Publicly scolding nurses who make minor math errors on drug calculations
options.D: Demanding blind obedience to rigid rules without question

explanation: Great leaders build psychological safety so nurses feel supported, motivated, and confident to do their best work.

question: Which of these is a great example of a positive feedback loop?

options.A: Insulin lowering high blood sugar back to normal
options.B: Parathyroid hormone raising low blood calcium levels
options.C: Oxytocin increasing uterine contractions during labor
options.D: Thyroid hormone stopping pituitary TSH production

explanation: Positive feedback pushes a process further and faster until the goal is met, just like oxytocin intensifying contractions until baby arrives!

question: What is the main goal of selecting patients for home delivery?

options.A: Maximizing maternal and newborn safety
options.B: Shortening the duration of labor
options.C: Promoting traditional herbs
options.D: Reducing hospital utility bills

explanation: The absolute priority in patient selection is ensuring the safety and health of both the mother and the newborn baby. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T9#GNS225_U3_T9_h2)

question: As a nurse, what simple and effective practice should you teach community members in areas with unsafe water?

options.A: Avoiding all handwashing to save clean water
options.B: Using untreated river water for infant formula
options.C: Boiling drinking water before consumption
options.D: Adding industrial solvents to kill local algae

explanation: Correct! Boiling is a cheap, reliable way families can kill germs at home when tap or well water isn't safe.

question: Why is proper technique so important when doing venepuncture?

options.A: To eliminate the need for hand washing
options.B: To reduce the cost of laboratory reagents
options.C: To prevent patient harm and protect sample quality
options.D: To speed up the patient discharge time

explanation: Taking your time to use the right technique keeps your patient safe from injury and ensures the lab gets an accurate, unblemished sample.

question: How does general palliative care differ from standard hospice care?

options.A: Palliative care is only provided in outpatient clinics, while hospice care is strictly for hospital inpatients.
options.B: Palliative care can be given alongside curative treatments, whereas hospice care begins when curative treatment has stopped.
options.C: Palliative care is managed entirely by physicians, whereas hospice care is run strictly by volunteers.
options.D: Palliative care focuses exclusively on spiritual counseling, while hospice care manages physical pain.

explanation: You nailed it! Think of hospice as a specific type of palliative care reserved for the final phase of life, while general palliative care can start on day one.

question: What exactly is colostrum?

options.A: The thick, yellowish first breast milk produced after birth
options.B: The primary protein supplement used to treat severe malnutrition
options.C: A local porridge made from fermented yellow maize
options.D: A traditional herbal drink given to calm crying babies

explanation: Colostrum is the super-nutritious, antibody-rich milk that comes right after delivery. Sadly, bad taboos sometimes cause mothers to throw it away—good thing you know better!

question: How does opening up the space between spinal bones help a patient with a pinched nerve?

options.A: It permanently fuses the spinal bones together
options.B: It stops blood flow to the nerve root
options.C: It stretches the spinal cord until it snaps
options.D: It reduces pressure on the compressed nerve

explanation: Think of it like giving the nerve some breathing room! When the bones are pulled slightly apart, the squeeze is lifted, easing pain and numbness.

question: A patient on long-term steroid therapy asks why they need a medical alert bracelet. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: It proves to your insurance that you take your pills.
options.B: It warns people around you that you might gain weight.
options.C: It lets emergency staff know your adrenal glands are asleep if you have an accident.
options.D: It stops doctors from giving you new prescriptions.

explanation: Spot on! In an emergency, medical staff need to know your adrenal system is suppressed so they can provide extra steroid support your body can't make on its own.

question: Which viral infection is strongly linked to causing cervical cancer in women?

options.A: Human immunodeficiency virus
options.B: Human papillomavirus
options.C: Epstein-Barr virus
options.D: Hepatitis B virus

explanation: High-risk strains of Human Papillomavirus (HPV) can cause cellular changes over time, which is why screening and vaccines are so important.

question: What term is used to describe shortness of breath that occurs specifically when a patient lies flat?

options.A: Tachypnea
options.B: Apnea
options.C: Bradypnea
options.D: Orthopnea

explanation: Orthopnea is breathing difficulty that worsens when lying down and improves when sitting upright. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T10#GNS213_U2_T10_h2)

question: Which blood type is known as the universal donor for red blood cells?

options.A: Type O
options.B: Type B
options.C: Type AB
options.D: Type A

explanation: Type O is a true lifesaver! Its red blood cells don't have A or B antigens on them, so recipient antibodies won't panic and attack them.

question: Where is the best spot on the finger to prick for a blood sample?

options.A: The direct center of the finger pad
options.B: The base of the fingernail bed
options.C: The soft skin right over the joint
options.D: The side of the fingertip

explanation: The sides of our fingertips have fewer nerve endings than the pads, making the prick much less painful for your patient.

question: Why is asking patients about their ability to afford basic needs important during a clinical assessment?

options.A: It proves whether the patient has a college degree
options.B: It guarantees immediate government financial grants
options.C: It helps uncover hidden financial strain affecting health
options.D: It replaces the need to check vital signs

explanation: Spot on! Many patients hide unemployment out of shame, so asking helps reveal financial stress that impacts their health and treatment. Well done! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T18#GNS225_U5_T18_h4)

question: Why do researchers process raw data in nursing studies?

options.A: To hide patient names to protect privacy
options.B: To increase the total number of study participants
options.C: To turn raw information into a structured, usable format
options.D: To write up the final hospital budget report

explanation: Great job thinking about research! Processing simply takes messy field notes or surveys and organizes them so you can actually study what they mean.

question: What is the medical term for a joint that cannot move at all?

options.A: Amphiarthrosis
options.B: Syndesmosis
options.C: Synarthrosis
options.D: Diarthrosis

explanation: You got it! A 'synarthrosis' is a fixed, immovable joint—just like the sutures in the skull protecting our brain.

question: What part of a research article should a nurse examine to check the study design and sample size?

options.A: Methodology
options.B: Author biography
options.C: Reference list
options.D: Abstract only

explanation: The methodology section details how the study was carried out, including who participated and how data was gathered. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h3)

question: What is an obsession in someone dealing with obsessive-compulsive neurosis?

options.A: A physical movement done to relieve muscle tension
options.B: An intrusive and unwanted thought that causes anxiety
options.C: A sudden memory loss regarding personal identity
options.D: A complete loss of contact with external reality

explanation: Spot on! Think of an obsession as an unwelcome thought or image that keeps popping into the mind against the person's will, bringing along a lot of stress.

question: Which muscle is a safe, standard site for giving an intramuscular DMPA injection?

options.A: Gastrocnemius muscle
options.B: Ventrogluteal muscle
options.C: Rectus abdominis muscle
options.D: Internal oblique muscle

explanation: The ventrogluteal site is a fantastic choice because it has a thick muscle mass safely away from major nerves and blood vessels.

question: You clear away some empty food cartons and clean paper towels from the nurses' station. Which bin should they go into?

options.A: Black or brown bin
options.B: Red cytotoxic container
options.C: Yellow bin with biohazard symbol
options.D: Yellow sharps safety box

explanation: Since paper towels and food wrappers are non-hazardous general waste, they belong in the ordinary black or brown bin.

question: A patient comes in with right upper quadrant belly pain, fever, and a history of dysentery. What condition should you suspect?

options.A: A perforated stomach ulcer
options.B: An amoebic liver abscess
options.C: Acute appendicitis
options.D: Severe kidney stones

explanation: Spot on! When the parasites travel up into the liver via the bloodstream, they can form a painful, pus-filled abscess.

question: Why can cultural stigma surrounding dementia make things especially tough for families in Nigeria?

options.A: It guarantees that traditional healers will cure the underlying brain damage
options.B: It forces the government to provide free nursing homes in every state
options.C: It eliminates all forms of physical illness in elderly community members
options.D: It can cause families to hide the affected relative and isolate themselves from support

explanation: Stigma creates shame and secrecy, which stops families from reaching out for the healthcare advice and community support they need.

question: Which of these is a common health problem that shows up after a major disaster?

options.A: Psychological trauma and PTSD
options.B: Increased availability of specialized surgeons
options.C: Immediate financial surplus
options.D: Enhanced community infrastructure

explanation: Great job! Survivors often deal with deep emotional distress and mental health challenges long after their physical wounds heal.

question: What is the most serious and dangerous complication that can happen after a gastrointestinal dilation?

options.A: Mild throat irritation
options.B: Temporary hiccups
options.C: Visceral perforation
options.D: Dry mouth sensation

explanation: Perforation means a tear or hole gets poked through the wall of the esophagus or bowel. It's a medical emergency that happens if the tissue tears during stretching.

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard criterion for patient selection before granting leave?

options.A: Presence of a supportive family or safe living arrangement
options.B: Having a large financial inheritance waiting outside
options.C: Demonstrated stability of acute psychiatric symptoms
options.D: Reliable cooperation with medication regimens

explanation: Money doesn't determine clinical readiness! Stability, safe housing, and taking medications are what truly matter for a successful leave.

question: A nurse notices women suffering from regular coughs and eye irritation because they cook daily with firewood in closed kitchens. What is the main culprit here?

options.A: A contagious bacterial lung infection spreading through handshakes
options.B: Indoor air pollution from inadequate ventilation and smoke
options.C: Severe vitamin deficiency caused by poor farming output
options.D: Direct allergic reaction to new insecticides used outdoors

explanation: Cooking with firewood in rooms without good windows traps heavy smoke inside, irritating the eyes and lungs over time.

question: What is the best position for a patient during a standard lumbar puncture?

options.A: Sitting straight upright with arms down
options.B: Lateral fetal position
options.C: Prone face down on pillows
options.D: Flat on the back with legs straight

explanation: You nailed it! Curling up on the side like a fetus opens up the spaces between the back bones.

question: What is a direct consequence of having weak vital data collection systems in a country?

options.A: Doctors will have less paperwork to complete daily
options.B: Citizens will stop falling sick from infectious diseases
options.C: Hospitals will automatically receive excess funding
options.D: Health planners rely on estimates that may lead to poor interventions

explanation: Inaccurate or missing data forces decision-makers to guess where resources are needed, resulting in poorly targeted health programs. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h6)

question: What do we call the mismatch when a baby's head is too big to fit through the mother's pelvis?

options.A: Uterine inertia
options.B: Secondary power failure
options.C: Occipitoposterior arrest
options.D: Cephalopelvic disproportion

explanation: Spot on! Cephalopelvic disproportion (CPD) simply means the baby's head size or the pelvis shape makes a normal vaginal delivery impossible.

question: What is a major cause of post-harvest food loss in farming communities?

options.A: Pest infestations and poor drying techniques
options.B: Strict international export inspections
options.C: Excessive government taxes on farm tools
options.D: Mandatory crop rotation laws from local councils

explanation: Bad storage, pests, and moisture can destroy a huge portion of crops right after harvest before they ever make it to market.

question: Which class of diuretics is known for being the most powerful at removing fluid from the body?

options.A: Potassium-sparing diuretics
options.B: Loop diuretics
options.C: Thiazide diuretics
options.D: Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors

explanation: Loop diuretics act on the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle, where a massive amount of sodium is normally reabsorbed, making them very potent. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T1#GNS223_U8_T1_h2)

question: What is the very first step a nurse should take after experiencing a needle-stick injury?

options.A: Fill out an official hospital incident report form
options.B: Wash the affected skin thoroughly with soap and running water
options.C: Squeeze the wound tightly to force out as much blood as possible
options.D: Wait until the end of the shift to see if swelling develops

explanation: Immediate washing reduces the viral load introduced by the sharp object before it establishes infection. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h7)

question: Why does a Quality Assurance Committee need members from different departments (multidisciplinary)?

options.A: To make committee meetings last longer
options.B: To reduce the number of doctors needed in the wards
options.C: Because government laws forbid single-profession committees
options.D: Because patient care involves many different health professionals working together

explanation: Spot on! Since nursing, pharmacy, and medicine all work together for the patient, everyone needs a voice on the team.

question: Why is regular multi-disciplinary follow-up essential for adults living with sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: To monitor and manage progressive long-term damage to major body organs
options.B: To perform routine blood transfusions that reverse the abnormal gene sequence
options.C: To prevent the patient from ever experiencing another painful crisis again
options.D: To ensure the patient takes daily antibiotics to cure the genetic mutation

explanation: Chronic organ damage to the kidneys, lungs, brain, and joints accumulates over years, requiring coordinated specialist care to catch and treat complications early. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h8)

question: Which stage of wastewater treatment relies mainly on physical screening and letting solids settle?

options.A: Primary treatment
options.B: Secondary treatment
options.C: Quaternary treatment
options.D: Tertiary treatment

explanation: Primary treatment is the first physical cleanup step. It uses large screens and settling tanks to catch big debris and let heavy particles drop out of the water.

question: What is the main job of our gastrointestinal (GI) tract?

options.A: Regulating body temperature and hormones
options.B: Pumping oxygenated blood to organs
options.C: Processing food and absorbing nutrients
options.D: Filtering waste products from the blood

explanation: Spot on! The GI tract's main assignment is to break down the food we eat, take in the good nutrients our body needs, and pass out the rest.

question: Which of these tools do you need on your clean workspace when mixing a topical dilution?

options.A: A standard household kitchen spoon
options.B: A clean mixing tile and spatula
options.C: A sterile surgical scalpel
options.D: A glass measuring cup for oral liquids

explanation: A clean flat tile and a spatula give you a nice, sanitary surface to blend your creams smoothly.

question: Which of the following is NOT permitted when managing an emergency patient who lacks capacity?

options.A: Refusing treatment based solely on the patient's unpaid hospital bills
options.B: Providing emergency life-saving interventions without a signed form
options.C: Inserting an intravenous line to administer emergency fluids
options.D: Performing a rapid head-to-toe physical examination for injuries

explanation: Emergency laws forbid turning away patients with urgent medical conditions based on their financial status or inability to pay. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T1#GNS315_U1_T1_h6)

question: Which mask is most important when doing a procedure that generates aerosols on a COVID-19 patient?

options.A: A standard cloth face covering
options.B: A disposable paper surgical mask
options.C: A simple clear plastic face shield alone
options.D: An N95 or higher respirator mask

explanation: That's correct! Procedures that create tiny floating mists require the tight seal and special filtration of an N95 respirator to keep you safe.

question: You notice a discharged stroke patient is confined to an upstairs room with no wheelchair access. What should you do?

options.A: Advise the family to keep the patient upstairs permanently.
options.B: Assess home modifications and refer the family to local social or disability support services.
options.C: Demand that the local government rebuild the entire house immediately.
options.D: Ignore the situation since the patient is already discharged from the hospital.

explanation: Spotting this barrier is great nursing observation. Your next step is to guide the family with practical advice and connect them to available support.

question: A toddler with diarrhoea drinks eagerly from a cup and seems restless. How would you grade this?

options.A: Severe dehydration
options.B: No dehydration
options.C: Some dehydration
options.D: Chronic dehydration

explanation: Spot on! When a child drinks eagerly and is a bit restless or irritable, it's a classic sign of moderate ('some') dehydration. They are thirsty and ready for ORS!

question: A healthy 50-year-old woman asks why she needs a routine mammogram when she feels fine. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Routine screening is legally required for all women over the age of forty in this country.
options.B: Screening tests catch cancer early before symptoms develop, which makes treatment more successful.
options.C: These tests are designed to prevent normal cells from ever mutating into cancerous growths.
options.D: Mammograms are only performed after a physician feels a distinct lump during a physical exam.

explanation: Screening is all about catching things early before they turn into bigger problems. Early detection makes treatment much easier!

question: A manager wants to introduce a new clinical audit system with minimal staff pushback. What is the best approach?

options.A: Install hidden security cameras in the nurses' station without telling anyone
options.B: Threatened immediate termination for anyone who questions the audit schedule
options.C: Involve frontline nurses in designing the standards and explain the safety benefits
options.D: Keep all performance data completely secret from the nursing staff

explanation: When you involve staff in the process, they build trust, feel valued, and truly understand why the safety controls matter.

question: When must a nurse researcher use non-parametric statistical tests?

options.A: When the research study is funded by a government hospital
options.B: When the data does not follow a normal bell curve distribution
options.C: When the sample size is extremely large and perfectly random
options.D: When all study variables are measured on a continuous scale

explanation: Brilliant! If your data is messy or skewed and doesn't fit that neat bell-shaped curve, non-parametric tests save the day.

question: Why do governments create food and nutrition policies?

options.A: To completely ban bringing any foreign food into the country
options.B: To control the exact daily price of goods in local markets
options.C: To manage employment records for all farm workers
options.D: To connect what farmers grow directly with what communities need to stay healthy

explanation: Food policies help make sure that farming output meets the actual nutritional health needs of the population. Great job thinking about the big picture!

question: Where does a prohormone usually get turned into its final, active hormone form?

options.A: Inside secretory vesicles as they wait to be released
options.B: Directly on the surface of the rough endoplasmic reticulum
options.C: Inside the cell nucleus during the transcription of DNA
options.D: Out in the bloodstream after the molecule leaves the cell

explanation: The final cutting and polishing happens right inside the storage bubbles (secretory vesicles) as the cell waits for the signal to release the hormone.

question: What is the main focus of a rehabilitation-focused day hospital?

options.A: Acute medical detoxification from alcohol and hard drugs
options.B: Providing emergency electroconvulsive therapy 24 hours a day
options.C: Strict physical containment of aggressive behavioral outbursts
options.D: Long-term skill building, socialization, and vocational readiness

explanation: Exactly! Rehabilitation centers help clients regain independence, learn practical skills, and get ready to return to work.

question: What is the very first thing an occupational health nurse should do when an injury happens at work?

options.A: File a lawsuit against the company owner
options.B: Calculate financial compensation for the worker
options.C: Assess the injury and provide immediate first aid
options.D: Conduct a drug test on all witnesses

explanation: You got it! First things first: always check the victim and give prompt first aid or stabilization before worrying about anything else.

question: How long must sleep troubles last to be diagnosed as chronic insomnia?

options.A: One month
options.B: Six months
options.C: Two weeks
options.D: Three months

explanation: You've got this! Doctors diagnose chronic insomnia when sleep issues happen at least three times a week and last for three months or longer.

question: A nurse wants to test a new pain reassessment workflow. Which of these is the best way to start a small-scale test?

options.A: Implement the workflow across all regional hospitals starting next Monday
options.B: Wait until next year when more funding becomes available
options.C: Test the workflow with three patients on the morning shift with one assigned nurse
options.D: Ask every nurse in the country to write an essay on pain reassessment

explanation: Spot on! Testing with just a few patients and a single nurse lets you see how the workflow feels in real life without creating chaos.

question: Why do clinicians often use resting metabolic rate (RMR) instead of basal metabolic rate (BMR)?

options.A: It completely excludes the energy used by internal organs
options.B: It is always identical to total daily energy expenditure
options.C: It measures the exact calories burned during running
options.D: It requires fewer strict laboratory conditions to measure

explanation: Great job! RMR is much more practical in hospital and clinic settings because it doesn't force the patient to go through a strict 12-hour fast and absolute rest like BMR does.

question: What requirement did government funding introduce for home health agencies?

options.A: Detailed documentation proving medical necessity
options.B: Mandatory ownership of hospital transport vehicles
options.C: Free medical care for all citizens regardless of age
options.D: Guaranteed 24-hour bedside nursing for every client

explanation: To get public funds, agencies have to write detailed reports proving that the patient truly needs skilled nursing care.

question: Who chooses the Village Health Workers to serve in rural communities?

options.A: The federal minister of health
options.B: The community members themselves
options.C: International donor agencies
options.D: Private pharmaceutical companies

explanation: Wonderful! When the community picks their own health worker, it builds instant trust and ensures the care fits their local culture.

question: Where is the safest spot to drop medicated eye drops into a patient's eye?

options.A: Into the lower conjunctival sac
options.B: Directly onto the cornea
options.C: Into the upper eyelid fold
options.D: In the inner corner of the eye

explanation: Gently pulling down the lower lid creates a nice little pocket (the conjunctival sac). Dropping it here prevents poking the sensitive cornea and keeps the medication right where it's needed.

question: What two physical measurements are required to calculate a person's BMI?

options.A: Waist and hip measurements
options.B: Height and skinfold thickness
options.C: Height and weight
options.D: Weight and waist circumference

explanation: The standard BMI calculation relies exclusively on an individual's height and total body weight. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T10#GNS121_U1_T10_h2)

question: What is a major health risk linked to certain traditional mineral-based treatments?

options.A: Sudden bone demineralization
options.B: Severe vitamin C overdose
options.C: Rapid muscle hypertrophy
options.D: Heavy metal toxicity

explanation: Unpurified local mineral remedies can sometimes contain dangerous heavy metals like lead or mercury. It is a great reminder why safety checks matter in patient care.

question: What is the main purpose of triage during a mass casualty disaster?

options.A: To collect insurance and payment details from victims
options.B: To sort and prioritize patients based on injury severity
options.C: To discharge healthy staff members so they can go home
options.D: To clean and disinfect the emergency room floors

explanation: Triage allows medical personnel to quickly identify and treat those with life-threatening injuries first when resources are limited. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h7)

question: What happens to the thickness of the placental membrane as pregnancy progresses toward term?

options.A: It stays the same thickness throughout pregnancy
options.B: It becomes thinner to improve exchange efficiency
options.C: It becomes thicker to protect against toxins
options.D: It disappears completely by the third trimester

explanation: As the fetus grows and needs more nutrients, the placental membrane thins out to shorten the distance substances must travel to cross over. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T7#GNS121_U6_T7_h2)

question: A study tests a stress-relief program for nurses in a busy city hospital. What is a great recommendation for future research?

options.A: Firing all city hospital nurses who reported high stress levels
options.B: Replacing human nurses with automated computer terminals
options.C: Testing if the same program works effectively in rural clinics
options.D: Stopping all future research on nurse mental health

explanation: Brilliant! Testing the same idea in a different setting helps us see if it works for nurses everywhere, not just in the city.

question: Why is boosting domestic revenue (like local taxes and insurance) so important for a sustainable healthcare system?

options.A: It reduces heavy reliance on unpredictable foreign donor funds and loans
options.B: It eliminates the need for professional nursing regulatory bodies
options.C: It stops patients from visiting hospitals for routine checkups
options.D: It guarantees that all private clinics become government-owned

explanation: Building internal financial strength gives a country independence, ensuring its health sector stays steady even if foreign grants change.

question: Which facility represents the primary level of mental health care in Nigeria?

options.A: University teaching hospitals
options.B: Local government health clinics and posts
options.C: State-owned general hospitals
options.D: Federal neuropsychiatric hospitals

explanation: Primary care is right at the grassroots level—the local health posts and clinics closest to our communities.

question: Why is detailed nursing documentation of a patient's nutrition care so important?

options.A: It guarantees the hospital gets zero complaints
options.B: It ensures continuity of care and creates a permanent record
options.C: It lets nurses prescribe their own diet orders
options.D: It replaces the need to give verbal shift handovers

explanation: Well done! Good charting keeps every nurse and team member on the same page across different shifts.
